title: allocation-footprint-variance-and-randomized-compaction-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a runbook-style set of notes capturing a set of focused experiments and telemetry observations aimed at explaining intermittent OOM events that correlate with high allocation churn and unusually wide allocation-footprint variance across requests. Goal is to capture reproducible test setups, hypotheses that were validated/invalidated, and suggested mitigations for a short-term hotfix and medium-term allocator improvements.

Background/context (brief):
- Symptoms seen in production pools: sporadic out-of-memory failures even though aggregate reserved pool headroom indicated ~10–25% free. Failures often follow short bursts of unusual request fanout (multiple parallel inferences + KV cache miss events).
- Notable signals: sudden jump in cudaMalloc retry latency, spike in reserved vs resident gap, free-run-length histogram shifts toward many small holes (~64–512B range) during burst windows.
- Existing runtime: hybrid slab + dynamic arena allocator layered over cudaMallocAsync with a fallback to cudaMalloc on rare misses. Workspace sizing is request-driven (estimated from token length + transient scratchpad multipliers).

Quick TL;DR findings:
- Fragmentation amplification most visible when small transient allocations (scratch buffers, per-token temporaries) are interleaved with a few very large allocations (KV cache restore, attention buffers). Small allocations create tombstones that prevent coalescing with adjacent freed large runs.
- cudaMallocAsync shows lower average latency but can hide deallocation ordering problems; deferred frees delay coalescing, causing spacer holes to persist longer than synchronous free would.
- Randomized, low-frequency compaction (forced synchronous free + small defrag pass) drastically reduces the 95th pct fragmentation ratio during synthetic bursts in our lab by ~35% with <5% additional tail latency in worst cases.

Experiment setups (repro):
- Baseline repro harness: local multi-worker harness that replays representative traces (trace id: replay-mem-burst-2024-09-27). Key knobs: parallelism (1..8), kv-cache-hit-rate (10..90%), per-request scratch-multiplier (0.5..2.0), chunk-size-dist (uniform, heavy-tailed).
- Measurement probes: nvprof/nsight to capture allocation/deallocation timestamps, custom telemetry to collect free-run-length histogram, resident vs reserved memory time-series, cudaMallocAsync retry counts, and per-allocation tag (small/large/kv/attention).
- Important command examples (what we ran):
  - nsys profile --output=mem-burst-repro.qdrep --trace=cuda --sample=none ./replay_harness --trace replay-mem-burst-2024-09-27 --parallel 6 --kv-hit 0.2
  - cuda-memcheck --leak-check full ./mini_alloc_test --pattern randomized
  - tail -f /var/log/redwood/runtime/allocator-events.log | grep "cudaMallocAsync retry"

Key observations (detailed):
1) Allocation footprint variance correlates with fragmentation pattern changes:
   - When per-request footprint variance (sigma/mean) > 0.6, the allocator free-run-length histogram shows a high-multiplicity of small free spans. These small spans are typically created by scratch buffers aligned to 64B boundaries and are insufficiently coalesced because adjacent big-run frees are not synchronized.
   - In short: high variance => interleaving of many small and few large allocations => tombstone-friendly layout.

2) Deferred frees from cudaMallocAsync exacerbate hole lifetime:
   - cudaFreeAsync (and backend async queues) move reclamation to later epochs. During a sustained burst, deferred frees stack up and prevent the fast coalescer from seeing contiguous free ranges.
   - On experiments where we forced synchronous cudaFree (wrapper) at low rates (1 in 50 frees), hole sizes collapsed faster and fragmentation metric improved.

3) Small-allocation amplification and alignment waste:
   - Many small allocations (<=1KB) are served from internal suballoc arenas. However we observed alignment padding rounding many of them up to 4–8KB when combined with arena headers, which multiplies waste.
   - Sorting allocations by size and choosing different suballocator bin boundaries shifted the histogram meaningfully. Reducing small-bin granularity reduced one class of persistent holes.

4) KV cache restore pattern is a frequent trigger:
   - Restores tend to call for a few very large contiguous blocks (multi-MB). If a restore happens concurrently with a phase of many tiny allocations, it will repeatedly fail to find a contiguous run and trigger cudaMalloc fallback attempts, increasing retry tail and causing higher memory pressure.

5) Randomized compaction shows promise as a pragmatic mitigation:
   - Implemented a low-risk mechanism in the harness: with probability p (0.02..0.1) after request completion, trigger a compact step that does: 1) synchronize worker free queue, 2) attempt local arena coalescing, 3) bump epoch to encourage cudaMallocAsync reclamation.
   - Results: p=0.05 gave best cost/benefit in tests: reduced median fragmentation by ~20% and 95th by ~35% for bursty traces, with per-request latency tail increases at the 99.9th pct of ~40–60ms depending on GPU generation. Worthwhile as a staged rollout.

Hypotheses tested (and outcomes):
- H1: "Changing cudaMallocAsync to synchronous cudaMalloc for all frees will fix OOMs." INVALIDATED — fixes some pathological cases but increases average malloc latency and increases tail for normal workloads; overall throughput drops ~8–12% in dense regimes.
- H2: "Adjusting slab bin sizes to coalesce more aggressively will reduce persistent holes." PARTIALLY VALIDATED — improved for small-allocation dominated traces but did not help mixed small+large traces without compaction.
- H3: "Introducing low-rate randomized compaction will reduce OOM incidence with minimal throughput cost." VALIDATED in harness and small-scale shadow cluster.

Short-term mitigations (actions we can roll quickly):
- Roll out randomized compaction p=0.03 to non-production and p=0.05 to canary pools; monitor fragmentation ratio and 99.99% tail latencies.
- Instrument allocator telemetry to expose: per-arena free-run-length histogram, counts of deferred frees, and per-request allocation variance metric. Add dashboards + alert if fragmentation ratio > 0.45 for >5min.
- Add a safety heuristic: when a large contiguous allocation (>=8MB) fails, trigger an immediate local compact attempt before falling back to cudaMalloc synchronous path.

Medium-term changes (engineering work):
- Improve coalescing algorithm to consider deferred-free epochs and proactively attempt to merge spans when adjacent pending frees are observed.
- Revisit slab bin boundaries and suballocator headers to reduce alignment blowup for very small scratch buffers; microbench before roll.
- Explore allocator hinting from higher layers: e.g., mark KV-restore as "high-contiguity preferred" and temporarily pause small-allocation arenas (drain to a reserved pool) during restore window.
- Long-term: research compaction strategies that avoid global syncs: block-local compaction + virtual address remapping, or use of CUDA memory pool APIs with bigger control over reuse.

Open questions and risks:
- Nightly sync compaction increases GPU idle cycles — what's the cost at scale? Need a 7-day cost simulation using real traces.
- Interaction with multi-tenant dedicated pools: fairness policies might amplify compaction tail effects for noisy neighbors.
- Stability across GPU generations and drivers (470 vs 535 vs future): we saw different reclaiming latencies and cudaMallocAsync behavior. Need cross-GPU regression matrix.

Immediate TODOs:
- [Ravi] Deploy randomized compaction to canary pool 3 (scheduled 2025-01-22) and capture pre/post dashboards.
- [Aisha] Add per-request allocation-variance metric to telemetry (deadline 2024-10-18).
- [Kenji] Run cross-driver matrix for reclaim latency (target matrix: T4, A10, H100 across drivers 510/525/535).
- [Marta] Draft a short internal postmortem template for any OOM incident that includes allocation variance and free-run-length histogram.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc mixes formal experiment outputs with quick field notes. Please add any missing reproducer scripts to the linked artifacts and mark things that should become runbook steps. If you think compaction probability p needs adjusting for specific customer pools (e.g., low-latency PLG vs background batch), note that in comments here.

Appendix (raw observation snippets):
- "Observed: cudaMallocAsync retry spike at t=2024-09-27T18:24:13Z correlated with kv-restore-start; reserved-resident gap jumped from 14% to 42% in 450ms."
- "Profiling: free-run-length hist pre vs post compaction: median hole size from 1.2KB -> 512B, mode from 256B -> 64B (indicates fewer medium holes)."
- Quick links to local repro: ./repro_suite/alloc_variance_run.sh --trace replay-mem-burst-2024-09-27 --compaction-p 0.05

-- end of notes --
